ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
1. Syncope with brief loss of consciousness. Referral to cardiology placed for evaluation of this episode.
2. Hypertension. Continue routine management and follow up as planned.
3. Hypothyroidism. Continue routine management and follow up as planned.

Breathing and tolerance of light activity were better than earlier in the stay, though she was advised that cough and fatigue could persist. She was able to understand and discuss the plan for completing treatment, monitoring symptoms, and arranging follow-up. She was not expected to return immediately to her full usual activity level and was advised to build activity gradually, with rest as needed. Her chronic hypertension and hypothyroidism remained relevant to routine ongoing care but did not prevent discharge. She was provided with guidance on symptoms that should prompt urgent assessment. The final plan was reviewed with her before leaving the hospital.

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
Complete the pneumonia treatment course according to the separate instructions provided at discharge. Rest as needed, drink fluids, eat as tolerated, and increase activity gradually as breathing and energy improve. Do not resume strenuous tasks until you can manage lighter activity without a significant increase in symptoms. Cough and tiredness may continue for a while, but should trend toward improvement. Contact a clinician if recovery stalls or symptoms return after improving. Seek urgent care for worsening shortness of breath, persistent or returning fever, confusion, inability to keep fluids down, or a sudden decline in your ability to manage daily needs. Continue the established plan for hypertension and hypothyroidism unless your regular clinician advises otherwise. Keep all discharge papers available for follow-up.

FOLLOW-UP:
Mara should arrange follow-up with her usual clinician after discharge to review recovery from pneumonia and confirm that symptoms are continuing to improve. The visit should also provide an opportunity to address routine care for hypertension and hypothyroidism and to clarify any questions about the separate treatment instructions. She should bring the discharge papers and describe any ongoing cough, breathlessness, fatigue, or difficulty returning to normal activities. If she cannot arrange timely follow-up, she should contact the hospital team for guidance. She should not wait for a routine appointment if breathing worsens, fever persists or returns, confusion develops, or she cannot maintain fluids.
